Design calls for James

  1. Hero wordmark removed. The header now carries the logo, so the white wordmark in the essay hero was a duplicate. Default: removed. The H1 now starts the hero, with a little extra top padding.
  2. Header over the dark hero. Default: the existing black header theme (data-header-theme="black", already in header.css) above the hero. It is #000 against the hero’s #121218, a barely visible step. While the draft banner is on, the banner sits between them; it goes away at publish. Alternative: make the hero #000 so the two read as one surface.
  3. Strip styling. Default: a light Neutral step 2 bar, not sticky (scrolls away above the sticky header). Source Code Pro eyebrow label, Inter text, instruction links ending in →, 44px icon dismiss. I added “ →” to the link text per the v15 instruction-link rule; the copy is otherwise exactly as briefed. At 390px it wraps to 3–5 lines (about 80px announce, 118px welcome). Alternative: a dark strip, which would merge with the black header.
  4. Porch layout. Default: dark stage (Neutral 7) above the homepage hero, two columns on desktop (5fr text / 7fr art), stacked on mobile with the art below. The primary button is “Read the essay →”. The porch title is an h2 styled like an H1, because the hero already has the page’s H1. The hero’s two buttons sit just below the porch, so two primary-style buttons can share a screen at some heights; say if the hero buttons should drop to secondary while the porch is up.
  5. Endcap. Default: three parts after the prose. “Tell us” on a dark stage with the page’s one primary button; “Keep going” as three outlined 6px cards with instruction-link lines; “Follow the lab” as the /updates signup embedded with a secondary button (so the page keeps one primary). Card sub-lines (“Read how →”, “Search the map →”, “See all research →”) are mine, not briefed. Alternative: drop the sub-lines and show the title only.
